messages.subject: Re: Sequenza failed >100 GB RAM
messages.body_plain:
I am sorry, it's hard to keep up with the replies :D.

We have located the issues with a bug in vroom, which is used by readr to read seqz files.
Originally it was more memory efficient to use readr vs the standard R i/o methods. The bug has not being addresses in years, so maybe I should think to add an option to use the readr or not, or find a way to avoid  the vroom memory issue

Best

messages.body_plain:
check for the sorting of the pileups, reference fa and gc file. They need to have the chromosome sorted in the same order, otherwise it will keep reading (skipping lines) to one file or the other until the end. alternatively, you could run 1 chromosome at a time (even in parallele) and merge the seqz files afterwards

messages.subject: Re: Negative Bf values
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emma,

Apologise for replying to this post with such delay, Are you sure the normal sample is matching? It seems there are very few common snps in the tumor. The Bf is calculated by a density distribution peak estimate, so it's possible if the values are so low, such as your case, that the value are negative. It doesn't make any sense, you are right, I haven't implemented in the code a round up to the bottom of the distribution, only around 0.5.

Thanks for reporting this

On Friday, May 26, 2023 at 3:43:13 PM UTC+2 Emma wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I've been running the Sequenza pipeline with no issues (first using bam2seqz with matched normal and tumour BAM files), however when I look at the results I seem to have some negative values for Bf - which seems impossible! Any ideas on whether something is going wrong here? I've attached my results file so you can take a look.
>
> Thank you,
> Emma
>
